I enjoy TFD quite a lot however there is a lot of grinding that is involved as RNG might not always be on your side when you either want to farm for a character or weapon. Granted you can fork over the money to buy characters however ultimate descendants alone can get up to $100+ but what you do with your money is completely up to you. The game is still very new and a lot of features are still being added and the games will have plenty of updates to come in the future for quality of life improvements so there is a future to look forward to. TFD is a labor of love now and into the future and personally that's the main reason why I'd stick with the game to see the community shift and grow with time as the game continues to flourish plus if you're someone who is not unfamiliar with games that make you grind then you won't have much issue integrating into TFD especially to those coming from Destiny 2 or Warframe. Overall the game is fun with a great community and well we can't really fault Nexon for still needing to make money to continue to fund the development of not only this game but any other games and your money is your money however the prices do get a little bit ridiculous but power to ya.

Let me start by saying this, a lot of people sound like they arent even grinding enough to get to the end game or get cool stuff before they quit.  I tried and tried, I have not spent a penny and ive got Ultimate Gley max module, Ultimate Valby max module, regular valby max module, enzo sharen etc all to 40, the only colossi i havent beaten yet is gluttony just because i havent really tried to find a team with my maxed ult gley yet.  I have 2 level 4 thunder cages all maxed module, i have the afterglow sword, and blue beetle etc etc... i have put time in and grinded out plenty of content BUT with that said:

The game lies about its drop rates.  They weigh certain drops way over what is advertised.  I have so many examples such as going 34 times in a row without getting a 20 percent chance thunder cage drop (0.05% .8^34) or rolling the worst trait on a gun 4 times in a row which is 1 in 38,000 (14^4) as well as 55 tries and counting on a 10 percent ult bunny drop (0.3% .9^55) which is why she isnt mentioned as an owned character above. Either i personally am the proof that the law of large numbers is false or after 177 hours its blatantly obvious they secretly weigh drop rates as to what is popular.  My play time has completely fallen off, i was playing this game like it was my job but I cant take the deceit anymore.  Which is sad cause the gameplay is pretty good, the characters despite being totally weeb and unimaginitive are still somehow charming in their own way most likely because the voice acting is really good and the level up and module system allows enough customization for some pretty solid replay value although you can get locked out of certain builds.  They have said they will address these problems in a future update by adding a trade in vendor for all the weighted drops you get and allow you to continue to level up your gun to add more module specs, but save yourself the trouble and avoid this game until then.  The company has already lost a lawsuit for another one of its games having deceitful drop rates.

Ngl, my review is kinda aimed at people coming from warframe, but somebody has to draw the parralels. For the most part it mirrors warframe. Monetization? Virtually identical, minus a smidge of fomo with improved character variants, and some harsher pricing (which isn't a concern for f2p players like myself anyways, and I advise others to do the same in all games aside from cosmetic purchases). Mod system that requires a degree in engineering? RNG that makes it too grindy to also balance having a life? Both are a check. They've even got their own take on the relic system. Although it's just better being kinda fun and less torturous because you open them by fighting bosses (although not always the really cool ones) instead of the same missions you did to get the relics in the first place. The guns are sorted and balanced in a way more akin to destiny and while they don't feel as good as destiny, are still miles better than warframe. Even the theme and story are just as almost but not really interesting as warframe except characters are more appealing (and easier to look at without a mild sense of disgust) than warframe just for being human beings in spite of poor voice acting. The thing the game struggles with most is performance (there's no reason a game should release on ps4, but a pc noticeably better than a ps4 that exceeds steam requirements should be having frame rate issues on the lowest settings) and just being new and therefore feeling a little small.

The First Descendant unfortunately offers nothing unique whatsoever aside from abhorrent microtransaction practices and fishy plagiarism from a company that has a similar track record compared to other shady Asian game studios like NetEase that create cobbled-together plagiarized games that have already seen massive success, only to shut these same games down months later after raking in the microtransaction payouts. Nexon has a history of shifting their main focus away from core gameplay and towards loot box systems and item drop rates that allow players to pay for better chances, without releasing what exactly those chances are themselves. Given that they were just recently fined $9 million in legal fees for misleading players of MapleStory in their other loot box system, I'm sure they are hard at work crafting a new way to rake in cash from a whole new First Descendant playerbase.

Every character looks as "anime-cool" as they can with no rhyme or reason, seemingly just to draw further emphasis on cosmetic options that players can buy with real money, further increasing their maximum payout. Apparently--with regard to the game's description on Steam--you are fighting for the survival of humanity. This coupled with the trailer as well as gameplay, showcases a product that comes out to being so incredibly generic. What truly gets under my skin is how much people eat this up. There is nothing epic about the clunky gameplay or uninspired futuristic soldier hullabaloo that we have seen from so many other uninspiring one-off games recently. I cannot emphasize how stiff everything in this game is. The whole project is an AI-generated Pinterest board of anime cyberpunk-soldier art that doesn't ever fit in its environment. How many more times in videogames does the protagonist or character we play as have to sit and stare and some emotionless being that reads through pages and pages of dialogue as blanket and shallow statements that we seemingly have to get attached to. Exposition should be shown to us, for us to uncover, rather than looking at generic burn mark scar-on-face friendly commander guy speak for 5 minutes in a monotone voice about the most randomly-named weapon or enemy ever and expecting us to care about it.

This game is once again so clunky and lacks any flow whatsoever, its way too uninspired with no new ideas. This game is obsessed with menus with an wholly terrible user interface, combined with a dead world with quest objectives written by an 8 year old child with the memory of a goldfish. This game is only appealing to those who like senselessly grinding and grinding away to be the best and look the best (except you can also be the best by spending exorbitant amounts of money). 

The only reason this game is pulling the numbers it has is because there is nothing else to play right now. What a poor mobile game on PC this is, unfortunately.

*I feel like I need to add that I do not hate microtransactions, this is a free-to-play game after all and the developers need to make money somehow. There are other, better ways to go about this though. Nexon clearly developed the store before their game, and their priorities are in the wrong place. Furthermore, this works to hate the player and find the best way to take their money fast before the game gets shut down.

Gonna be straight up, I thoroughly enjoyed this game. Obvious jank and seemingly rigged drop rates aside [that's just probability in a nutshell, bro~]. In short form it's a good game worth playing through at least once and especially if you have friends [up to 4 including you] to go through it with.

Long time now~
Redeeming qualities!
- It's hella fun to grapple all over the place, especially since you can work that rope into your attacks.
- Speaking of the melee attacks you can use it to dive bomb legit anything [negating fall damage] and 9/10 times it's gonna be hella powerful.
- Weapon structuring is quite nice, in that all the weapons work differently even within their own classes. Each SMG works different than every other SMG but they're all still SMGs, for example~
- Ammo systems work well with 4 types and it makes you think about what kind of weapons you should bring into the fight with you. I'd love to have an LMG and auto-pistol but they both use standards and I'd run out of ammo. Forced me to think about and try new weapon types out of my comfort zone.
- Several descendants to choose from and I hear more on the way, each having their own attribute and skills which stay within the character's theme. Poisoner deals in tick damage and traps, lightning user is constantly on the move, grenadiers work on thinning the little guys, etc.
- Free to play, pay for cosmetics, good for everyone, no?
- Several hours of playtime with very little grinding necessary [unless you want a certain descendant or gun] goes well for feeling like you're making good progress and you're always able to get assistance from the community for that one part you know you'll get stuck on [Dead Bride Pain] and you can get extra cosmetics and cool titles by redoing missions so +replayability~
- Landscape, maps and character personality feels good and it's enjoyable to grapple around and explore them all. Each map distributed into multiple sections and 3 different factions populating them, all having their own attributes and the occasional dotting of elite or enhanced enemies serve a good focus point for challenging encounters and end-mission markers.
- The multiplayer has high potential and I believe is done quite well, although significantly dulled by difficulties in connection, and I thoroughly enjoy that you can assist other players mid-mission although I wish it was done through pop-ups instead of interactions so I don't join someone's mission simply by defending myself.

Not so redeeming qualities...
- Most of the cool stuff is locked behind a paywall, no money = Basic life
- Most descendants are locked behind late-game, you'll probably be playing bunny 60% of the game.
- The other two unchosen descendants from the tutorial become inaccessible until mid-game, so free to play dudes will have a hard time getting more than two of the optional descendants for hours into the game. 45hrs into the game and 5hrs after beating the main story, I finally got my 4th descendant.
- The difficulty spike doesn't start until late game and it gets steep when you notice it, compounded by connection issues and rubber-banding makes it hard to play sometimes. Manageable as long as you keep a reasonable distance from your party members on most occasions, but it can get bad during the obstacle courses in some operations & some optional missions.
- Why must the shotguns use the ammunition hardest to come by? They aren't strong enough to make use of the ammunition you need to save up to fire it, and there's only two weapon classes utilising the specials where it would much more easily fit into. It feels like such a waste of a beloved weapons class...
- Story seems thought up in a single night and it seems like a disappointingly high let-down in such a well thought-out landscape and setting.
- Most of the UI is hard to wrap your head around and I don't have the slightest idea on what half of what I picked up did, but it's nice to be able to check where each item drops in the research lab and everything makes more sense the more you experiment so it was nice to have when I actually had patience to work it out.
- The game itself is rather hard on my system, especially in the loading screens. I had to relaunch after the tutorial loading screen crashed 3 consecutive times and no longer launches after the most recent update. Might be more of a personal issue, but eh...

All round though, I recommend giving it a try. Don't know til ya give it a go, after all~

Its a good 3'rd person looter shooter, don't have to grind for 100+ hrs for something you want either.

Good graphics, tolerable parkour, decent gunplay.  Don't bother if you care about story, or having  your time/money respected.

Also? How about we make it so that (at the VERY least) when queue'd in solo - you don't have the fight become active long before players get control of their character. Loading in with 2 deaths in pocket is unnecessary and sloppy.

Movement system is stiff af. It feels limiting, animations are slow and boring, grappling hook has very short range and limited surfaces/objects it can be used on, with a long wind up time, so if you happen to be falling off a ledge and shoot it up - you will fall anyway. All that in a game that makes you move constantly to avoid damage or reach another objective. 

Shooting is just meh. It's there, there is something that tries to be recoil, guns feel mostly the same all around. Enemies don't react much to being hit at all.  

Boss fights are basically the same with every boss. Shoot some small weak spots, while boss spams AOE atatcks, teleports and goes through it's phases. Balance work in such a wonderful way that facing the boss alone (or with one friend) is easier than with a full squad of random players. Add to this stiff movement system and mediocre shooting and boss fights turn into a chore. 

Monetization is a bit insane. Most descendants are hidden behind a lot of grind, to complete which you need to unlock all maps first. Skins cost a lot. Changing color costs per color per each color slot on a skin. And all colors are one-time use. Oh, and you can't paint standart skin. Only the ones you buy from the shop. No free looks or colors. Some skins are available only for a limited time. You get the picture.

Story and characters are as generic as they can get. Generic bad guy trying to conquer you world, while a voice in your head (Guide) tries to help you find magical item and stop him. Characters all speak and behave more or less in the same way. Same goes to fan-service and looks - your usual bood windows and tough guys, without any notable or unique features.

Good Game, especially considering it is from Nexon. I do warn that it is a very heavy grind for items you want, with sometimes abysmal drop rates. I think that the game will continue to grow and become more refined!

If you're a fan of action RPGs, The First Descendant is a game you can't miss. This exhilarating title combines intense combat, a compelling storyline, and stunning visuals to deliver a gaming experience that stands out in its genre.

The game immerses you in a beautifully crafted world filled with diverse environments and a rich lore that keeps you engaged from start to finish. The combat mechanics are fluid and satisfying, offering a perfect balance between strategy and fast-paced action. With a wide array of characters to choose from, each with unique abilities, the gameplay feels fresh and exciting every time you dive in.

One of the standout features of The First Descendant is its cooperative multiplayer mode. Teaming up with friends to tackle challenging missions and formidable bosses adds a layer of depth and enjoyment that is hard to find in single-player modes. The game also boasts an impressive progression system, rewarding players with meaningful upgrades and customization options that keep you invested in your character's development.

In summary, The First Descendant is a must-play for anyone who loves action-packed RPGs. Its engaging gameplay, beautiful world, and cooperative multiplayer make it a standout title that promises hours of fun and adventure.
